costs.title: How we build your sea freight rates
costs.intro: Our sea freight quotes are based on objective parameters (volume, weight, trade lane, seasonality, carrier capacity and cargo type) to stay aligned with the market while securing your flows.

cards.title: Which factors drive the price?
cards.text: Volume (m³) and weight, departure and arrival ports, service type (FCL or LCL), cargo nature (standard, dangerous goods, reefer), seasonality and available capacity with carriers. Based on this, we select the most suitable service for your budget and lead times.

cards.title: How to get an accurate quote?
cards.text: The more complete your request, the more accurate the quote: cargo description, volume or dimensions, total weight, origin/destination country and city, preferred Incoterm, approximate value and time constraints. We use this information to compare several FCL/LCL options and departure ports (France/Benelux).

cards.title: How to avoid unexpected price increases?
cards.text: We clearly detail what is included in our offer (sea freight, surcharges, THC, pre‑/post‑carriage) and the validity period of the quote. Upfront, a clear Incoterm choice and compliant documentation help reduce costly surprises linked to storage, inspections or customs.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions – B2B & international moves
faq.q1: I’m a company: how does sea freight France–Angola work for my pallets and B2B cargo?
faq.a1: For companies, we build your France–Angola quote based on a few key elements: cargo type, volume in m³ or number of pallets, weight, departure/destination ports or cities and desired lead times. We then compare FCL (full 20'/40' container) and LCL (groupage) to optimize your costs and lead times, include customs clearance and cargo insurance, and organise pickup, pre‑carriage, ocean leg and, if needed, final delivery.
faq.q2: I’m planning an international move to Angola: how does shipping my personal effects and vehicle work?
faq.a2: For an international move, we first estimate your volume in m³ and the nature of your goods (boxes, furniture, appliances, vehicle, motorbike, etc.). Depending on this volume, we recommend LCL groupage or a dedicated 20'/40' container. We support you with packing, loading, export/import formalities, ad valorem insurance and tracking until the container arrives in Luanda. You have a single point of contact to coordinate the whole process.
faq.q3: How can I track my container in transit?
faq.a3: We provide a tracking number and access to our web platform for real-time tracking from loading at the departure port to arrival at the destination port. You receive updates on key milestones and are informed in case of any transit disruption.

faq.a: To cover risks of damage, loss or theft on high-value and sensitive flows (international moves, vehicles, B2B cargo). An ad valorem policy protects your cash flow and contractual commitments along the whole journey.

faq.q: Which shipments should be prioritised for insurance?

claims.title: In case of a claim: the right steps
steps: Inspect the container and cargo as soon as it is opened and take clear photos of any damage or shortages (inside/outside, package numbers, seals).
Write detailed, precise reservations on the delivery document or BL, indicating which packages are affected and the nature of the damage.
Inform us as soon as possible and send the key documents: BL, commercial invoice, packing list, photos, written reservations and any survey report.
Keep the original packaging and do not destroy damaged items before the insurer or appointed surveyor has given clearance.
Cooperate with the appointed surveyor (if any) and keep us updated so we can defend your interests with the insurer.
